# Fleet run token accounting — method and baseline (2026-07-19/20)

**Kind:** measurement artifact — **no runtime code.** Not read at skill runtime.
**Generated by:** claude-opus-4-8
**Subject run:** one `/wf:fleet` invocation over an umbrella that decomposed into two
sub-tasks (SM-2, SM-3), shipped end-to-end to merged PRs.
**Companion:** [wf-token-leak-inventory.md](./wf-token-leak-inventory.md) — the defects
this baseline exposed.

This is the reviewable baseline for what a fleet run actually costs and, more
importantly, **how to measure one correctly**. The measurement method is the load-bearing
part: the obvious way to read the transcripts over-reports by ~2x.

## 2. Method — and the trap

> **The transcript writes one JSONL record per _content block_, not per assistant
> message.** Every record in a group repeats the **same** `usage` object, and
> `output_tokens` is a running count that only reaches its true value on the **last**
> record of the group. Summing raw records double-counts cache figures.

Observed directly in `agent-a24d59cc01e8dff8c.jsonl` — one message, four records:

```
rec  out     cc      cr   blocks
 11    3  12159   68879   thinking
 12    3  12159   68879   tool_use
 13    3  12159   68879   tool_use
 14    3  12159   68879   tool_use
 15    3  12159   68879   tool_use
 16  443  12159   68879   tool_use
```

That is **one** API call — 68,879 cache-read tokens, 443 output. Counting records gives
six. In that agent alone, 57 of 97 message ids repeat.

**Correct method:** group records by `message.id`, take the **max** of each usage field
per group. Never sum; never take the first (that undercounts `output_tokens`).

The inflation factor is **not uniform** — it ranged 1.7x–3.8x per agent (mean 2.37x)
because tool-heavy messages split into more blocks. So naive summation distorts
*rankings*, not just totals: audit lenses inflated most (2.4–3.8x), ship orchestrators
least (1.74x).

Reference implementation:

```powershell
# Per-transcript totals, deduped by message.id
$msgs=@{}
foreach($l in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $path)){
  if(-not $l.Trim()){continue}
  try{$o=$l|ConvertFrom-Json}catch{continue}
  if($o.type -ne 'assistant' -or -not $o.message.usage){continue}
  $u=$o.message.usage; $k=[string]$o.message.id
  $v=@([int]$u.input_tokens,[int]$u.cache_creation_input_tokens,
       [int]$u.cache_read_input_tokens,[int]$u.output_tokens)
  if($msgs.ContainsKey($k)){
    $e=$msgs[$k]; for($i=0;$i -lt 4;$i++){ if($v[$i] -gt $e[$i]){$e[$i]=$v[$i]} }; $msgs[$k]=$e
  } else { $msgs[$k]=$v }
}
# then sum $msgs.Values
```

For tool-call inventories, apply the same idea keyed on the `tool_use` **block id** —
otherwise a multi-block message reports its tool calls several times.

Pricing used throughout (Claude Opus 4.8): input $5/M, output $25/M, cache write
$6.25/M (1.25x), cache read $0.50/M (0.1x). Costs are **API-equivalent** — the run
itself may have been billed under a subscription.

## 3. Corrected baseline

| | tokens | cost |
|---|---|---|
| cache read | 112.4M | $56.21 |
| cache write | 6.76M | $42.25 |
| output | 641.3K | $16.03 |
| input | 11.6K | $0.06 |
| **total** | | **$114.55** |

1,145 real assistant messages (from 2,522 raw records). 51 subagents + 1 orchestrator.
Two tasks. **Every agent ran `claude-opus-4-8`.**

Per task: SM-2 $53.11, SM-3 $55.89 — near-identical, so this is the shape of the
pipeline, not one task going pathological. Fleet orchestrator itself: $4.80.

For contrast, the naive record-summing figures were 229M cache read / 17M cache write /
~$235. If you see numbers near those, the dedup step was skipped.

## 4. Cost by pipeline phase

Audit lenses are counted under **verify**, which is where the registry dispatches them.

| phase | agents | msgs | cost | % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| verify | 24 | 405 | **$37.16** | 33.9% |
| ship orchestration | 2 | 262 | **$33.67** | 30.7% |
| implement | 2 | 173 | $16.46 | 15.0% |
| qa | 4 | 64 | $5.45 | 5.0% |
| plan | 5 | 60 | $4.42 | 4.0% |
| triage | 3 | 39 | $3.81 | 3.5% |
| spec | 4 | 38 | $3.42 | 3.1% |
| pr | 3 | 41 | $3.15 | 2.9% |
| finalize | 2 | 26 | $1.71 | 1.6% |
| classify | 2 | 5 | $0.50 | 0.5% |

Two readings worth carrying forward:

- **Verifying cost 2.3x more than implementing** ($37.16 vs $16.46). Verify splits almost
  exactly in half — $18.65 across 15 lens agents, $18.51 across 9 verify-spec/verify-fix
  agents.
- **Verify + orchestration = 65% of spend.** Everything that produces a deliverable
  (spec, plan, implement, pr) totals $27.45, or 25%.

Split by task, showing the re-audit:

| phase | SM-2 | SM-3 |
|---|---|---|
| verify | $14.28 (9 agents) | **$22.88 (15 agents)** |
| ship orchestration | $20.26 | $13.41 |
| implement | $9.13 | $7.33 |

SM-3's verify cost 60% more purely because the fix-and-recheck loop re-fired all five
lenses (15 verify agents vs 9).

> The `plan` row includes 3 index-row bookkeeping agents swept in by role matching. Plan
> proper is 2 agents, ~$3.3.

## 6. Top individual agents

| agent | msgs | inflation | cache read | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ship SM-2 | 174 | 1.74x | 24.0M | $20.26 |
| Ship SM-3 | 88 | 1.80x | 8.0M | $13.41 |
| Implement SM-2 | 97 | 2.14x | 12.4M | $9.13 |
| Implement SM-3 | 76 | 1.71x | 9.5M | $7.33 |
| verify-spec SM-2 | 54 | 2.41x | 5.7M | $5.18 |
| verify-spec SM-3 (re-run) | 49 | 2.24x | 5.2M | $4.07 |
| verify-spec SM-3 | 34 | 2.38x | 3.5M | $3.84 |
| verify-fix SM-3 | 34 | 1.91x | 3.2M | $2.50 |

**Ship SM-2 alone is 18% of the session.** Its context grew 43K -> **422K** across 174
messages, averaging ~134K per turn — every turn re-reading the accumulated history.

Ship SM-3 is the cache-TTL case: only 8.0M of reads but $13.41, because most of its cost
is cache *writes*. It ran 23:52 -> 02:08, so the 5-minute cache TTL kept expiring between
turns and it re-paid the 1.25x write premium.

Fixed per-agent boot tax, measured on the smallest agent
(`agent-a37e7f328797d52da.jsonl`, classify SM-3): ~41K of context to produce **231
output tokens**.

---

## 7. Caveats

- **Costs are API-equivalent**, computed from transcript `usage` fields at list prices.
  They are not an invoice.
- **Single run, n=2 tasks.** Ratios (verify:implement, orchestration share) are
  suggestive, not established. Re-measure before treating them as targets.
- **Role bucketing is regex over agent descriptions** and is approximate at the edges —
  see the `plan` caveat in §4.
- **Session logs are machine-local and prunable.** Every number here is reproducible only
  while the transcripts in §1 exist.
- ~13% of raw `cache_creation` volume sat on records with `output_tokens <= 1`. Those are
  first-blocks of multi-block messages, not retries — the dedup in §2 handles them
  correctly. An earlier reading of this doc's data mistook them for aborted API calls.
